NoteDown keeps all notes — open and closed — in one Markdown file, plus
one file of the same format per set of people notes are shared with
(`docs/sync-and-sharing.md`). The file must stay pleasant to read and edit in any other Markdown editor
(Obsidian, a plain text editor), so the metadata is hidden in one HTML
comment per note, which Markdown renderers don't show.

Implemented in `app/js/core/notes-file.js`, tested in `tests/core.test.mjs`;
`app/sample/notes.md` is a complete example.

## Structure

```markdown
<!-- note id=s01 status=open created=2026-10-13T08:05Z modified=2026-10-13T08:40Z due=2026-10-13 -->
## Weekly groceries
- [x] Oat milk
- [ ] Coffee beans (the Ethiopian ones)

<!-- note id=s13 status=closed created=2026-10-10T09:00Z modified=2026-10-13T07:30Z closed=2026-10-13T07:30Z -->
## Pay the electricity bill
Done by bank transfer, reference number in the banking app.
```

- A note starts at its marker line `<!-- note … -->` and runs until the
  next marker or the end of the file. Its body is plain Markdown and may
  contain any headings, so the marker — not a heading — is the boundary.
- Text before the first marker is the file's preamble (e.g. a title); it
  is kept unchanged.
- When writing, notes are separated by one blank line and the body is
  trimmed; the order of the notes in the file carries no meaning (the
  app sorts).

## Marker attributes

| Attribute | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Stable and unique across all files, as notes move between them (no spaces) |
| `status` | yes | `open` or `closed` |
| `created` | yes | Time in UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ` |
| `modified` | yes | Time (UTC) of the last content change (closing or reopening doesn't count) |
| `due` | no | Date `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `closed` | when closed | Time (UTC) the note was closed |
| `left` | no | Shared files only: identity IDs of members who left the note, comma-separated (see "Leaving a shared note") |

**Times are stored in UTC** (the `Z` suffix), so devices and members of
a shared file in different time zones agree on them; each device shows
them in its own local time ("Today 10:05" in Berlin for `08:05Z`).
`due` is a calendar day without a time zone — due on the 17th is the
17th wherever the device is. A time without `Z` (older files) is read as
the device's local time.

Unknown attributes are ignored when reading. A marker without `id` gets a
new one; a missing `created`/`modified` falls back to the other.

## Moved notes

When sharing moves a note into another file (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md`),
the old file keeps a marker without body, so a concurrent edit follows
the note instead of reappearing here:

```markdown
<!-- note id=s03 moved=2026-10-13T09:00Z -->
```

`moved` is the time of the move (UTC); markers are written after the
notes and dropped 30 days after the move. Other editors don't show them.

## Device names

The private file names the user's devices, one marker each after the
moved markers, so every device of the identity shows the same names
while the server knows none:

```markdown
<!-- device id=Qm9vS2V5SWQxMjM0NTY3OA name=Chrome%20on%20Windows -->
```

`id` is the device ID from the device list (`docs/server-api.md`), `name`
is percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`). A device names itself when it
turns on sync or restores; a linked device writes the name the new
device's QR code suggests; removing a device drops its marker. Merging
works per ID: the side that changed a name wins, a removal stays. Any
text after a device marker is dropped, like after a moved marker.

## Leaving a shared note

A member can't write the file of the remaining members (it isn't one of
them), so leaving only marks the note in the shared file:

```markdown
<!-- note id=s11 status=open created=2026-10-12T10:00Z modified=2026-10-13T08:00Z left=VG9tSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY -->
```

The leaver's devices hide the note at once. The first device of a
remaining member that syncs the file moves the note into the file of the
members without everyone in `left` (created on first use, like sharing;
with one member left it becomes that member's private note) and drops
`left`; the old file keeps a moved marker as usual. Merging takes the
union of both sides' `left`. Decided 2026-10-14 over a marker the leaver
writes elsewhere: the note stays readable for the others until one of
them moves it, which is the leaver's choice anyway.

## Members

A shared file names its members with their own display names, one
marker each after the moved markers, so a member who isn't a contact of
everyone still shows by name:

```markdown
<!-- member id=U2FtSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Sam -->
```

Each member's devices write only their own marker (the user's display
name, percent-encoded) and keep it current; merging works per ID like
device names. A contact keeps the name the user gave them; a member who
isn't a contact shows with this name in a neutral color (decided
2026-10-14 over "Unknown").

## Contacts

The private file also holds the user's contacts, one marker each after
the device markers, so every device of the identity has the same
contacts and names while the server only knows pairs of identity IDs
(`docs/server-api.md` → "Contacts and invitations"):

```markdown
<!-- contact id=TGVhSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NQ name=Lea color=2 -->
<!-- contact id=VG9tSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Tom color=4 pending=2026-10-14T09:00Z -->
<!-- contact id=U2FtSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Sam color=5 server=https%3A%2F%2Fnotes.example.org%2Fapi -->
```

`id` is the contact's identity ID, `name` the name the user gave the
contact (percent-encoded; the contact's own display name is the
suggestion), `color` the avatar color slot 1–6. `server` is the contact's
home server (the API address, percent-encoded; absent = the default
server, the app's configured API address). `pending` marks a
request this user sent that the other side hasn't confirmed yet (the
time it was sent, UTC); it is dropped once the server lists the pair.
Merging works per ID like device names: the side that changed a contact
wins, a removal stays. Any text after a contact marker is dropped.

## Custom order

A file can hold one order marker, after the device and contact markers: the note ids
of a custom order, first to last (backlog #24):

```markdown
<!-- order modified=2026-10-14T09:00Z ids=s04,s01,s07 -->
```

In the private file it is the user's own **Custom** order: ids from any
of the user's files (ids are unique across files), so shared notes can be
ordered without the other members seeing it. In a shared file it is the
circle's **Shared order** (backlog #25), listing that file's notes and
set by any member. `modified` is the time of
the last change (UTC); without `ids` the order is empty. Ids of notes
that no longer exist are dropped on the next save. Merging takes the list
the changed side wrote, the newer one when both changed it. Other editors
don't show the marker; any text after it is dropped, like after a moved
marker.
